description: Auto-discovered mappings for Super Mario Bros. (World).nes

0x24.name: sky_fill_blank (BG pattern table $1000, i.e. CHR $124)
0x24.notes: Nametable tile $24 fills all empty sky area in SMB 1-1. The BG uses pattern table $1000, so the on-screen tile is CHR $124, which is all zeros -> every pixel is palette index 0 ($22 periwinkle in palette 0). Note CHR $024 (sprite pattern table) is a different, sloped shape, so the picker's tile_id 36 must be read against the BG table.

0x00 (CHR 0x100).name: HUD/score digit '0' (slashed zero)
0x00 (CHR 0x100).notes: Background CHR 0x100 = a 5x6 slashed zero. Nametable 0 row 3 cols 4-8 and 12-14 hold tile 0 (palette 2), i.e. the score/coin digits, rendered white ($30) on the backdrop. Any palette-2 slot-1 edit recolors all HUD text. Tile read shows the glyph; nametable read confirms the placement.

0x25.name: solid_fill_slot1 (cloud body)
0x25.notes: CHR $125 = all pixels palette index 1. Under BG palette 2 that is $30 white, so it is the cloud interior; clicked at (148,58). Generic solid fill: it takes whatever colour slot 1 of its palette holds.

0x35-0x3C.name: big_cloud_tile_set (palette 2)
0x35-0x3C.notes: Nametable 1, 1-1 big cloud = rows 6-8, cols 23-30 (screen box (117,48)-(179,71)). $35 left edge, $36/$37 alternating top bumps (row 6), $25 body fill (row 7), $38 right edge, $39 bottom-left corner, $3A/$3B bottom scallops, $3C bottom-right corner. Body index 1 = $30 white, outline index 3 = $0F black.

0x53-0x56.name: question_block_2x2 (palette 3)
0x53-0x56.notes: 16x16 ? block quadrants: $53 top-left, $54 top-right, $55 bottom-left, $56 bottom-right. Index 1 = $27 orange face, 2 = $17 brown dashes/glyph, 3 = $0F black border. The 1-1 block at NT1 cols 12-13 rows 10-11 (screen (29,80)-(44,95)) was clicked at (41,82) on $54.

0x60-0x6A.name: warp_pipe_tile_set (palette 0)
0x60-0x6A.notes: Green pipe in 1-1 at NT1 cols 24-27, rows 22-25 (32px wide, 32px above ground, screen x 125-156). Row 22 = $60-$63 rim top (rounded corners), row 23 = $64-$67 rim lower, rows 24-25 = $68,$69,$26,$6A shaft ($26 carries the black/green shading under the lip). Index 1 = $29 lime green, 2 = $1A green, 3 = $0F black. Clicked tile was $64 at (132,184), rendered $29.

0x70-0x73.name: goomba 2x2 sprite tiles (16x16)
0x70-0x73.notes: Sprite pattern table. Goomba = 4 x 8x8 OAM entries, 2 wide x 2 tall (16x16), palette 7. $71 is the mirror of $70 (top half: brown dome + black eye), $73 mirrors $72 (bottom half: brown + peach feet). SMB draws a blank top row of $FC when it emits the 3-row form. OAM slots rotate every frame, so slot numbers change; identify by position+tiles.

0x20-0x27.name: big Mario 2x4 sprite set (16x32)
0x20-0x27.notes: Super Mario is 8 x 8x8 OAM entries in a 2-wide x 4-tall grid = 16x32. In this frame: rows y=163/171/179/187 at x=68/76 with tiles $21/$20, $23/$22, $25/$24, $27/$26, all h-flipped (facing left), palette 4. $25 = body tile (red $16 with black/olive detail). Small Mario would be only 4 entries.

0xFC.name: blank sprite padding tile
0xFC.notes: All 64 pixels transparent. SMB emits it as an OAM entry to pad short sprites to the row count its object handler uses (seen as the top row of Goomba entries at y=185). Also used as the OAM y=$F8 "off-screen" sprite.

0x69.name: pipe shaft highlight stripe (2nd column)
0x69.notes: CHR $169 = solid palette index 1 with a 1px index-2 seam at column 5. Under BG palette 0 that is $29 lime green with a $1A green line, so it is the pipe's bright face. Stacked 4 rows tall in tall 1-1 pipes (NT0 cols 12-15 rows 22-25); the connected slot-1 run is 5 px wide x 32 px tall = 160 px. Slots 1-3 of BG palette 0 are all in use on screen, so it cannot be isolated by a tile edit.

0x2E.name: HUD coin icon (background)
0x2E.notes: CHR $12E = a 4x7 oval: face index 1, right edge index 3. Placed in nametable 0 at (11,3) (screen x 88-95, y 24-31) as part of the fixed status bar. Its attribute block is BG palette 3, so it renders $27 orange face + $0F black edge; clicked (91,27) sampled rgb(234,158,34) = $27. Only 24 px of that slot are in view, so a BG palette 3 slot-1 edit hits the coin and any ? block on screen, nothing else.

0xFF.name: HUD coin sprite (behind background)
0xFF.notes: Sprite tile $FF, only rows 5-6 have pixels (a few dark pixels at the coin's base). Emitted as OAM #0 at (88,25), sprite palette 7, behind_background = true, so the background coin tile $2E covers it and it is normally invisible. Palette 7 is therefore shared between the Goomba and this HUD coin sprite. Do not treat OAM #0 as a Goomba.

0x08-0x17.name: big Mario pose sets (facing right)
0x08-0x17.notes: Unflipped (attr 0) 8-tile blocks: $08-$0F and $10-$17 are two poses of the same 2x4 16x32 stack, both palette 4. Seen at (112,177)-(127,208) while walking right; $0C/$14 are the middle-left body tiles (red $16 with $18 dark shading). SMB1 stores left/right poses as separate tiles (turn 2's left-facing Mario used $20-$27 with every OAM entry h-flipped).

0x29.name: HUD "x" of the coin counter
0x29.notes: CHR $129 = an X shape in palette index 1. Sits at nametable 0 (12,3) next to the coin tile $2E, in an attribute block with BG palette 2, so it renders $30 white. The following tile $00 (CHR $100) is the digit 0.

chr:0x153.name: ? block 16x16 metatile tile-id table entry (TL/TR/BL/BR = $53/$54/$55/$56)
chr:0x153.notes: PRG ROM source of the four 8x8 tile ids that make the 16x16 ? block. A table at prgRom 0xC80 (CPU $8C80), 4 bytes per 16x16 metatile (9 entries, 0xC80-0xCA3; followed by the palette blocks at 0xCA4); the ? block entry is 4 bytes at 0xC8C = 53 55 54 56 = $53,$55,$54,$56, stored in the order TL,BL,TR,BR. On screen in World 1-1 the ? block at NT1 col 25/26 row 10/11 sampled as TL=$53 (205,86), TR=$54 (211,86), BL=$55 (205,94), BR=$56 (211,94), all BG palette 3. There is a second identical entry at 0xC90. Proof (search and ledgered write): write_memory prgRom 0xC8C = $24 (sky) -> ledger seq 1 in hack eval-sheet2-tiles, reason '? block entry first tile $53 -> sky'; reset_emulator, Start + hold Right ~150 frames into 1-1, pause; screenshot showed every ? block on screen with its top-left quadrant replaced by sky; undo_edit restored $53 and a later level load showed the block whole again.

rom_origins.notes: ? block 4-tile entry in the 16x16 block metatile tile-id table; table base 0xC80, stride 4
32-byte level palette block starts at 0xCCB (BG palettes 0-3 then sprite palettes 4-7); BG palette 0 slot 1 is at 0xCCC and was changed $29 -> $16

1.name: overworld ground/brick BG palette
1.notes: SMB1 World 1-1. Entry values [0F,36,17,0F]: index 1 = brick highlight (originally $36 peach, verified by writing $12 bright blue and seeing the top highlight line of the ground brick row turn blue at y=224), index 2 = brick brown ($17). Ground brick tile 181 (and 180) sample with palette_id 1.

0 (background).name: pipe_bush_hill_green + shared sky backdrop
0 (background).notes: World 1-1: slot 1 = $29 lime green (pipe/warp-pipe body), slot 2 = $1A green (pipe shading), slot 3 = $0F black (outline). Slot 0 = $22 periwinkle, the universal backdrop written at $3F00: every background palette renders index 0 as this colour, so it is the whole sky. Clicked pipe pixel (132,184) renders $29.

2 (background).name: cloud_white (white body, black outline)
2 (background).notes: Slot 1 = $30 white (cloud body), slot 3 = $0F black (1px outline, sampled on the big cloud at (119,60),(135,49),(150,70) = rgb 0,0,0), slot 2 = $21 sky blue. Palette RAM slot 0 reads $0F but the PPU renders index 0 as the $3F00 backdrop $22 periwinkle.

3 (background).name: question_block_orange
3 (background).notes: Slot 1 = $27 orange (block face), slot 2 = $17 brown (rivet dashes and ? glyph), slot 3 = $0F black (block border). Used by the 16x16 ? block: tiles $53/$54 (top half) $55/$56 (bottom half). Palette RAM slot 0 reads $0F; index 0 renders the $3F00 backdrop $22.

7 (sprite).name: goomba (brown body, black eye, peach feet)
7 (sprite).notes: Sprite palette 7 = $0F, $0F, $36 peach, $17 brown. Slot 3 brown = Goomba body, slot 1 black = eye, slot 2 peach = feet/underside; slot 0 is transparent for sprites. Sampled at (221,196) = rgb(153,78,0) = $17 on the left 1-1 Goomba.

4 (sprite).name: mario (red cap/shirt, skin)
4 (sprite).notes: Sprite palette 4 = $22, $16 red, $27 orange (skin), $18 dark olive-brown (hair/shoes). Sampled at (75,182) = rgb(181,49,32) = $16 on Mario's body. Mario sprites are h-flipped when he faces left.

small_mario_standing.notes: PRG ROM source of the four 8x8 tile ids that make small Mario's standing frame (sprite pattern table $0000, sprite palette 4). The table holds 8 bytes per frame: 4 tile ids used by small Mario (row-major TL,TR,BL,BR) plus 4 bytes that are $FC blank padding in the small-Mario frames. Small Mario's standing frame is the 4-byte run at prgRom 0x6ED3 = 3A 37 4F 4F = $3A,$37,$4F,$4F; the next frame (walk/airborne $9E,$9E,$9F,$9F) is at 0x6ECB, so the frames are 8 bytes apart (0x6E83, 0x6E8B, ... 0x6ED3, 0x6EDB...). Emulator observation before the edit: small Mario standing at the start of 1-1 emitted OAM entries tile $3A at (40,193) TL, $37 at (48,193) TR, $4F at (40,201) BL, $4F h-flipped at (48,201) BR, with two $FC blank padding rows above; when he was mid-air the frame switched to $9E,$9E,$9F,$9F, matching the 0x6ECB entry. Proof (search and ledgered write): write_memory prgRom 0x6ED3 = $FC (blank) -> ledger seq 1 in hack eval-sheet2-tiles; reset_emulator, Start, wait ~3.5 s for 1-1 and Mario to stand; pause; list_sprites then showed OAM index 5 (Mario's top-left) as tile $FC while $37/$4F/$4F were unchanged, and the screenshot showed his upper-left tile missing. undo_edit restored $3A.

0x075A.description: player_lives_counter: stores lives minus one (a 3-life game starts at 2) and decrements by one per death; the "WORLD 1-1 x N" card shows value + 1. Found by blind differential search (29 then 3 survivors over two deaths) and proven by writing 5 and watching the card follow; session b3d6d3a5, 2026-10-06.

0x0086.description: player_x_position (Mario horizontal position in the level): Encoding: one byte, the level x-coordinate modulo 256; it is the coordinate the engine scrolls the level in, so it wraps at 256 as the 256-pixel screen scrolls (observed 251 -> 9 during a run). Mario's on-screen x is derived in ROM routine at CPU $F171: LDA $0086 (indexed), SEC, SBC $071C (scroll), STA $03AD. Proof (differential + write): snapshot_memory/play_input/diff_memory narrowed holding Right from 167 to 41 survivors, $0005/$03AD/$0755/$0086 all tracking screen x; the writer of $03AD was disassembled to $0086 - $071C; then write_memory $0086 = 200 (0xC8) while paused and stepping frames moved Mario from screen x=40 to x=200 (screenshot: Mario standing at the right-hand bush instead of the start hill). Writing the derived copies $03AD/$0755 alone had no effect (snapped back), so $0086 is the master. No separate player page byte was found: the level page is tracked only by the scroll $071C and the nametable. Source: differential search.

0x00CE.description: player_y_position (Mario vertical position): Encoding: one byte, the screen y of the top of Mario's sprite box; on the ground in 1-1 it reads 176, and it decreases as Mario rises (jump) and increases as he falls. Proof (differential + write): diff s3->s4 with filter 'decreased' after holding A for 10 frames showed $00CE 176 -> 141 (a copy moves with it at $03B8, 176 -> 141, and Mario's OAM y entries $0204/$0208 176 -> 141); then write_memory $00CE = 120 (0x78) while paused and stepping 2 frames left Mario hanging in mid-air at y~120 (screenshot: Mario floating in the sky above the bushes instead of standing on the ground). Source: differential search.

0x075F.description: world_number: Encoding: the current world number, 0 = World 1, so World 1-1 holds 0. Proof (write + screenshot of the death card): in World 1-1, $075F read 0; write_memory $075F = 4 (together with $075C = 2), then held Right ~300 frames to die and let the card draw; the resulting screenshot showed both the fixed HUD and the black card reading 'WORLD 5-3' (world digit 5 = 4+1, level digit 3 = 2+1). The two values were distinct in the two positions, which fixes which address is world and which is level. Source: differential search / own judgement for a value that does not change by playing.

0x075C.description: level_number: Encoding: the level number within the current world, 0 = the first level of the world, so World 1-1 holds 0. Proof (write + screenshot of the death card): $075C read 0 in 1-1; write_memory $075C = 2 (with $075F = 4), died by holding Right, and the 'WORLD 5-3' card screenshot confirmed the second digit is this byte (2 -> 3). Kept as the level number, not the world, because the two test values appeared in the positions matching their addresses. Source: differential search / own judgement for a value that does not change by playing.

0x071C.description: screen_scroll_x (level's left edge, mod 256): Supporting variable found while chasing the horizontal position. $03AD (Mario's on-screen x) is computed as $0086 - $071C in the ROM routine at CPU $F171, so $071C is the x of the level's left edge (scroll) modulo 256. Watched during a hold-Right run: it climbed 1,6,14,24,38,...,119 and froze at 119 while Mario was blocked at a pipe at $0086=63 (screen x = 63-119 = 200). It does not wrap with Mario's byte (the two are on different 256-pixel pages once Mario has crossed one). Source: differential search.

0x03AD.description: player_screen_x (derived on-screen x of Mario): Derived copy: ROM routine at CPU $F171 does LDA $0086,X / SEC / SBC $071C / STA $03AD,Y, so $03AD = player_x ($0086) - scroll ($071C) = Mario's x on the visible screen. Written every frame (trace_writes on $03AD gave PC $F17F, prgRom 0x717F, 60 writes in 30 frames). Writing $03AD directly has no effect: after write_memory $03AD = 200 and stepping one frame it was back to 40. Do not use it to move Mario; write $0086 instead. Source: differential search plus disassembly.

0x07ED.description: coin_count_display: The two-digit coin counter shown after the coin icon ('x'), two BCD bytes: 0x07ED = tens, 0x07EE = ones. Found with no reference by differential search: a ? block coin increments only the ones digit, so a diff 'increased' (c0->c1, 264 survivors) filtered 'equals 1' left 32 including 0x07EE (old 0 new 1); the repeat coin (1 -> 2, 'x01' -> 'x02') filtered 'equals 2' left 17 including 0x07EE (old 1 new 2). Proof by write: wrote 0x07ED/0x07EE = [5,5] (would display x55), then collected one coin; the HUD redrew to x56 - the tens 5 is exactly what was written and the ones ticked 5->6, and RAM read back [5,6]. The display only redraws on a change, so the coin had to be collected after the write. Companion binary counter (not displayed) at 0x075E.

0x07F8.description: level_timer_digits: The TIME countdown, three BCD bytes, most-significant first: 0x07F8 = hundreds, 0x07F9 = tens, 0x07FA = ones. In World 1-1 the paused HUD read TIME 310 and RAM read [3,1,0]. Found with no reference by differential search while Mario stood still: snapshot t0, 150 idle frames, snapshot t1, diff 'decreased' left 21 survivors including 0x07F9 (8->7) and 0x07FA (4->3); a second 150-frame round with from=dt1 narrowed to 6 including 0x07F9. Proof by write: wrote 0x07F8-0x07FA = [5,0,0] (500), the game's own tick decremented it once, and the screenshot HUD showed TIME 499 (naturally it was at 099). The timer only redraws its digits on a tick, so the write must be followed by one tick.

0x006D.description: player_x_page: Page byte (high byte) of Mario's horizontal position in the level. Encoding: Mario's absolute level x = 0x006D*256 + 0x0086, where 0x0086 is the low byte (the byte that wraps at 256); each unit of 0x006D is one 256-pixel screen. Found with no reference by differential search. Watching memory while holding Right: as 0x0086 ran 249,250,252,253,255,0,2,3 the byte 0x006D went 0,0,0,0,0,1,1,1 - it increments on exactly the frame 0x0086 wraps 255->0. Walking back left, 0x0086 went ...1,0,255,254... and 0x006D went 1->0 on the same wrap frame. snapshot_memory/diff_memory across one crossing (a->b) kept 54 'increased' survivors including 0x006D (old 0, new 1); the reverse crossing (d->e, filter 'decreased' from d1) narrowed to 24 survivors with 0x006D (old 1, new 0). Disassembly confirms it is not the scroll: the player-position update at CPU $BF40-$BF46 is STA $0086,X ; LDA $006D,X ; ADC $02 ; STA $006D,X (carry added into the page byte), and the left-edge clamp at CPU $B013-$B021 copies the camera's 16-bit position into $0086/$006D (camera high at $071A, low at $071C). Proof by write: with Mario mid-level (0x0086=205, camera $071C=93) I paused, wrote 0x006D=1 and 0x0086=5; after stepping frames RAM still held 0x006D=1 (not zeroed) with 0x0086=5 and camera 98, i.e. absolute x 261, and the screenshot showed Mario at on-screen x~163 (right-hand side, by the hill/Goomba) rather than the left edge, where a page-0 value (abs 5 - camera 98 = -93) would be clamped. Writing 0x006D alone while it leaves Mario off-screen makes the game's clamp rewrite 0x0086=scroll and 0x006D=0, so the low byte must be written to match. This corrects the older 0x0086 entry's claim that 'no separate player page byte was found': 0x006D is that byte. Companion low byte: 0x0086.

0x075E.description: coin_count_binary (0-99; reaching 100 gives a 1-UP): Binary coin counter, separate from the two BCD HUD coin digits at $07ED/$07EE. The coin routine $BBFE does INC $075E at $BC0C, LDA $075E / CMP #$64 at $BC0F-$BC14, and if it reaches 100 does STA $075E=0 / INC $075A ($BC16-$BC1B) to grant an extra life. Observed: after one ? block coin, $075E=1 while $07EE=1. Found by disassembling the routine reached from the coin caller; the only PRG operands referencing $075E are inside $BBFE.

0x07DD.description: score_digits: The displayed MARIO score, six BCD bytes most-significant first: 0x07DD = millions, 0x07DE = hundred-thousands, 0x07DF = ten-thousands, 0x07E0 = thousands, 0x07E1 = hundreds, 0x07E2 = tens. The ones digit is a fixed '0' tile, so the HUD shows seven digits. Found with no reference by differential search: collecting a ? block coin adds exactly 200, and a diff 'increased' (c0->c1, 264 survivors) filtered 'equals 2' left 15 addresses including 0x07E1 (old 0 new 2); the repeat coin on the restarted level (1 coin -> 2, score 200->400) filtered 'equals 4' left 3 including 0x07E1 (old 2 new 4). Proof by write: wrote 0x07DD-0x07E2 = [1,2,3,4,5,6], then collected a coin; the HUD redrew to 1234760 - the written digits 1,2,3,4,6 appear and only the hundreds digit moved 5->7 for the coin's +200, read back as [1,2,3,4,7,6]. The HUD redraws the score only when it changes, so a write needs a score-changing event (a coin) to appear.

0x074E.description: area_palette_index: Index into the area-palette selector table $85BB (=$01,$02,$03,$04), read by LoadAreaPalette at $85BF. World 1-1 holds 1 -> selector 2 -> the overworld palette block at $8CC8. Found with no reference: read 1 throughout World 1-1 play (play_input watch) and the value read from the table during the 1-1 reload was $85BC (=$85BB+1) = 2.

0x0773.description: vram_buffer_selector: Selects which buffer the NMI's VRAM transfer ($8EDD) copies. The NMI reads $805A,X and $806D,X with X=$0773 and drops the result into $00/$01. Entries: 0 -> $0301, 1 -> $8CA4, 2 -> $8CC8, 3 -> $8CEC, 4 -> $8D10 (four [3F 00 20 <32 palette bytes> 00] palette blocks), 5 -> $0300, 6 -> $0341 (RAM buffers). The NMI clears it to 0 every frame at $80DB, so it is a one-frame request. Found with no reference: trace_writes on $0773 for 600 frames showed 598 writes of 0 from PC $80DE (the NMI clear) plus a single nonzero write from the level-init palette step; the pointer tables were read from PRG at $805A/$806D.

notes: SMB splits the scroll at scanline 31: the HUD above is fixed, the playfield below scrolls (recorded 2026-10-05 as an address entry by mistake; moved here by hand).

player_horizontal_position_pair: Mario's level x is 16-bit: page 0x006D + low 0x0086: Correction to the existing 0x0086 'player_x_position' entry, which says 'no separate player page byte was found'. There IS one: 0x006D is the page/high byte and 0x0086 is the low byte; absolute level x = 0x006D*256 + 0x0086. Evidence (differential search, no reference): 0x006D 0->1 on the exact frame 0x0086 wrapped 255->0 walking right, and 1->0 on the reverse crossing; the player update at CPU $BF40-$BF46 adds the carry into 0x006D; and writing 0x006D=1 with 0x0086=5 moved Mario to absolute x 261 (screenshot screen x~163). Also note the game clamps: if a page edit leaves Mario off the visible screen, CPU $B013-$B021 rewrites 0x0086 and 0x006D from the camera's 16-bit position ($071A high, $071C low).

hud_value_extents: HUD counter extents proven by one-byte-past probes: Extent probes for the three World 1-1 HUD counters (differential search, no reference). Score: wrote 0x07DC..0x07E4 = [9,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8] then collected a ? block coin. RAM read back [0,1,2,3,4,7,6,7,8] and the nametable score row showed tiles [1,2,3,4,7,6,0] - my 0x07DD..0x07E2 digits 1,2,3,4,6 displayed (5 -> 7 for the coin's +200) but 0x07E3 = 7 did NOT appear; the 7th displayed digit stayed the fixed '0' tile. So the stored score is exactly 0x07DD..0x07E2 (six BCD bytes, millions..tens) and the HUD draws a fixed 0 ones digit after it. Coin: wrote 0x07EC..0x07EF = [9,5,5,8] then collected a coin; RAM [9,5,6,8] and the HUD showed x56 - 0x07EC=9 and 0x07EF=8 were not displayed, so the coin display is exactly 0x07ED (tens) / 0x07EE (ones). Timer: wrote 0x07F8..0x07FA = [5,0,0] and the HUD followed to 499, the three visible TIME digits.

level_start_palette_chain: How a level's colours reach the PPU (World 1-1 example): Chain proven with no reference. Level-init state machine $8567 (LDA $073C / JSR $8E04, table $856D) step 9 -> $85BF (LoadAreaPalette): LDY $074E / LDX $85BB,Y / STX $0773. Table $85BB = $01,$02,$03,$04; 1-1 has $074E=1 so $0773=2. Next NMI ($80B6-$80C3): LDX $0773 / LDA $805A,X / STA $00 / LDA $806D,X / STA $01 / JSR $8EDD. The pointer tables $805A/$806D map selector 1..4 to the four PRG palette records $8CA4,$8CC8,$8CEC,$8D10, each [3F 00 20 <32 palette bytes> 00]. $8EDD/$8E92 writes the record: STA $2006 (=$3F) / STA $2006 (=$00) then loops LDA ($00),Y / STA $2007 for the 32 bytes, setting all 4 BG + 4 sprite hardware palettes. Evidence: trace read on $85BB during a 1-1 reload = PC $85C5 reading $85BC value 2; trace read over $8CA0-$8D27 during a reload = PC $8E96/$8E9C/$8EBB/$8EE2 reading $8CC8-$8CEB; manual write $0773=1 then step_frame changed the whole palette to $8CA4 (screenshot), $0773=2 restored it. The live PPU palette for 1-1 equals the $8CC8 block (with $3F00 backdrop $22 written by the record's first byte being $0F and the engine's own backdrop write).

statusbar_text_table: Top status bar fixed-text VRAM-buffer table (MARIO, WORLD, TIME): PRG source of the fixed HUD words along the top of the screen. It is a WriteVRAMBuffer record stream: each record is [PPU addr hi, PPU addr lo, length, tiles...] and the buffer ends with a 0x00 first-byte terminator. Record 1 at prgRom 0x752: 20 43 05 then tiles 16 0A 1B 12 18 = 'MARIO' at nametable $2043 (row 2, col 3); record 2 at 0x75A: 20 52 0B then 20 18 1B 15 0D 24 24 1D 12 16 0E = 'WORLD  TIME' at $2052 (row 2, col 18); terminator 0x00 at 0x76B. Letter tiles: M=16 A=0A R=1B I=12 O=18 W=20 L=15 D=0D T=1D E=0E, blank=24. Proof: write_memory prgRom 0x755 (MARIO 'M' 16) -> 20 ('W'), ledger seq 1, reset_emulator, screenshot of the title screen HUD read 'WARIO'; undo_edit restored 16. The card's WORLD text is a different table (see world_card_text_table), so this edit did not touch it.

world_card_text_table: WORLD-card text record ('WORLD 1-1' intro/death card): PRG source of the black card that shows 'WORLD 1-1' after Start / on death. Record header at prgRom 0x783 is 21 4B 09: PPU address $214B = nametable 0 row 10, col 11, length 9. Data at 0x786: 20 18 1B 15 0D 24 24 28 24 = 'WORLD' + blank + a placeholder byte + '-' (28) + a placeholder byte; the world/level digits are patched into the two placeholder positions at runtime (observed card = WORLD 1-1 with 01 28 01). Confirmed the card position by reading nametable 0 while the card was up: row 10 cols 11-15 = 32 24 27 21 13 ('WORLD', same letter tiles as the HUD) and cols 17-19 = 01 28 01 ('1-1'). Proof: write_memory prgRom 0x786 (card 'W' 20) -> 16 ('M'), ledger seq 1, reset_emulator, pressed Start, screenshot showed the card read 'MORLD 1-1' while the top HUD still read 'WORLD 1-1'; undo_edit restored 20.

0x91CD.name: LoseLife - take a life away when Mario dies
0x91CD.notes: Found with no reference by trace_writes on the lives counter $075A while holding Right from the start of 1-1 into the first Goomba: the ONLY writer was PC $91DC (prgRom 0x11DC) with value going 2 -> 1 - that PC is the BPL immediately after DEC $075A at $91D9. Disassembling backwards, the previous RTS is at $91BC and $91BD-$91CC is a data/jump-table region, so the routine's first instruction is $91CD: INC $0774 ; LDA #$00 / STA $0722 ; LDA #$80 / STA $FC ; DEC $075A. The instruction that does the job is DEC $075A at $91D9. On the path where Mario still has lives the BPL at $91DC branches forward to $91E9 (the world/level setup that draws the next life); if the byte underflows (game over) $91DE-$91E8 clears $0772=0 and sets $0770=3 then RTS. No direct JSR/JMP targets $91CD (searches for '20 CD 91', '4C CD 91', 'CD 91' and '91 CD' found no call/pointer; the one 'CD 91' byte pair at CPU $B05B is inside a data table), so the caller was not pinned down - it is reached by the game's indirect dispatch. Proven: after the trace RAM $075A read 1 and the following screenshot showed Mario respawned at the start of 1-1.

0xBBFE.name: AddCoin - collect a coin (coin count + coin digits, +200 score, 1-UP at 100)
0xBBFE.notes: Entry $BBFE, RTS at $BC48 (0x4B bytes). Found with no reference: the mapping's coin digits $07ED/$07EE have NO direct PRG operand anywhere, so the increment had to be through a helper; searching PRG found the block/coin caller's JSR $BBFE at CPU $BB7D (prgRom 0x3B7D) and a free-coin JMP $BBFE at CPU $DE0B (prgRom 0x5E0B, from the coin-collect routine $DE03), and disassembling confirmed the code. What it does: $BBFE LDA #$01 / $BC00 STA $0139 sets the BCD operand's ones digit to 1; $BC03 LDX $0753 / $BC06 LDY $BBF8,X loads Y=$17 when $0753=0 (table $BBF8 = $17,$1D); $BC09 JSR $8F5F (the shared digit helper) adds 1 to the 6-digit counter $07D7+Y, target $07E9-$07EE, so it increments the coin ones digit $07EE with carry into the tens $07ED. $BC0C INC $075E is the binary coin counter; $BC0F-$BC14 LDA $075E / CMP #$64; at $BC16 STA $075E=0 and $BC1B INC $075A grants the extra life at 100 coins. $BC22 LDA #$02 / $BC24 STA $0138 and $BC2D JSR $8F5F add 200 to the score; $BC36 JSR $8F06 plays the coin sound; $BC39-$BC43 spawn the floating '200' popup at $02FB. Proven in the emulator: a jump into the first 1-1 ? block gave score 000200 (digit '2' at $07E1), coin count $075E=1 and coin digits $07ED/$07EE = [0,1] (HUD 'x01'). The write PC for the digit update is inside the helper (see $8F5F), not in this routine, because the coin digits are written by the shared helper.

0xB74F.name: DecrementTimer - count the level TIME down
0xB74F.notes: Found with no reference from the mapping's timer digits $07F8-$07FA. trace_writes on the BCD operand byte $0139 for 300 frames returned writes of $FF from PC $B792 (plus $8F83, the helper clearing the operand) exactly 12 times in 300 frames - one tick every ~24 frames, matching the visible countdown. $B792 is the JSR that follows STA $0139 at $B78F. Disassembly gives the routine entry $B74F (the JSR at $AF35 calls it; searching PRG for JSR $B7xx found that call site - the bytes at $B74B-$B74E are data, and $B74F is LDA $0770). What it does: LDA $0770 / BEQ $B7A3 (returns unless $0770 != 0); checks game mode $0E >= 8 and != $0B and $B5 < 2; returns while the divider $0787 != 0, otherwise sets $0787 = $18 (24) - this is the 24-frame tick divider; then LDY #$23 / LDA #$FF / STA $0139 / JSR $8F5F. The instruction that does the job is STA $0139 = $FF at $B78F: it loads the shared digit helper $8F5F with operand $FF (signed -1) and Y=$23, so the helper subtracts 1 from the 6-digit counter based at $07D7+$23, i.e. the timer digits $07F8/$07F9/$07FA. The caller is the JSR $B74F at CPU $AF35 (prgRom 0x2F35). When the timer reaches zero it runs the time-up path at $B79A: STA $0756 ; JSR $D931 ; INC $0759.

0x8F5F.name: AddBCD - shared signed-digit adder for the HUD counters (coin/timer/score)
0x8F5F.notes: Entry $8F5F, main RTS at $8F86 (40 bytes; carry tail through $8F95). Found by trace_writes: watching the self-ticking timer digits $07F8-$07FA for 400 frames returned exactly one writer, PC $8F78 (prgRom 0x0F78) with 51 writes - that PC is the DEY immediately after the STA $07D7,Y at $8F75, i.e. this routine. What it does: it adds the 6-byte operand at $0134-$0139 (most-significant first, ones digit at $0139) to the 6-byte counter based at $07D7 whose ones digit is $07D7+Y (the caller passes Y, so the target range is $07D7+(Y-5)..$07D7+Y). $8F6C ADC $07D7,Y / $8F75 STA $07D7,Y do the work; digits are signed so $FF acts as -1 (borrow: $8F87 DEC $0133,X / LDA #$09) and a sum >= $0A carries (SEC / SBC #$0A / INC $0133,X / JMP $8F75 at $8F8E). $8F7C-$8F86 clears the operand $0133-$0139 (plus a guard on $0770). Callers found by searching PRG for JSR $8F5F: CPU $B792 (timer/hurry; LDY #$23 then STA $0139=$FF so it SUBTRACTS 1 from the timer, target $07D7+$1E..$23 = $07F5-$07FA, the timer digits $07F8/$07F9/$07FA at the top), CPU $BC09 and $BC2D (coin routine $BBFE - Y from table $BBF8=$17 for $0753=0 targets $07E9-$07EE, so the coin digits are updated here, and Y from $BBFA=$0B adds the 200 score), and CPU $D32E/$D33F (time-up bonus). Because the coin routine, the timer and the score all call this one routine with different Y offsets, it is the helper shared by several counters.

0x8000.name: Reset - power-on / RESET entry (boot, init, then idle loop)
0x8000.notes: Where the CPU starts at power-on. Found by read_memory of the 6502 RESET vector: $FFFC/$FFFD = $00 $80 -> $8000. Disassembly of $8000 shows the canonical boot sequence: $8000 SEI / $8001 CLD (mask IRQs, clear decimal); $8002 LDA #$10 / $8004 STA $2000 (PPUCTRL, NMI off while initializing); $8007 LDX #$FF / $8009 TXS (stack to $01FF); $800A-$8013 LDA $2002 / BPL twice (poll PPUSTATUS to wait two vblanks for PPU warm-up); $8014-$8029 checks the continue marker $07FF == $A5 and picks the boot state via $90CC; $802E STA $4011 (APU DMC); $8031 STA $0770; $8036 STA $07FF=$A5 and $8039 $07A7=$A5 (write the resume markers); $803E LDA #$0F / STA $4015 (APU enable); $8043 LDA #$06 / STA $2001 (PPUMASK, both layers on); $8046 JSR $8220 / $8049 JSR $8E19 (init); $804C INC $0774 (frame counter); $804F-$8054 LDA $0778 / ORA #$80 / JSR $8EED (enable NMI); $8057 JMP $8057 - the routine hands control to an infinite wait loop where the CPU idles and all per-frame work happens in the NMI (the game is NMI-driven; the main thread never leaves $8057). The instruction that ends the boot job is the transfer to the idle loop at $8057. Emulator proof: reset_emulator, then get_cpu_state returned PC $8057 (with a fresh cycle counter and the title screen restored) - i.e. the CPU had run the code at $8000 and settled exactly on the JMP $8057 target. Before the reset the emulator was also sitting at $8057/$8058 during normal play, confirming the main thread stays in this loop. No direct JSR/JMP to $8000 exists; the RESET vector is the only entry, as expected.

0x8082.name: NMI - per-frame interrupt handler (PPU setup, OAM DMA, game logic)
0x8082.notes: The vblank/NMI handler, i.e. the whole per-frame engine. Found by read_memory of the 6502 NMI vector: $FFFA/$FFFB = $82 $80 -> $8082. Disassembly $8082-$8181 (ends RTI at $8181, 0x100 bytes) shows what it does each frame: $8082 reads $0778, AND #$7F, stores, AND #$7E / $808C STA $2000 (PPUCTRL: nametable select + sprite size, NMI bit cleared during setup); $80A3 STA $2001 (PPUMASK from $0779); $80A6 LDA $2002 (read PPUSTATUS, reset the vblank/sprite-0 latch); $80B3 LDA #$02 / STA $4014 (OAM DMA page 2 -> hardware sprites); $80B6-$80C3 indexes tables $805A/$806D by VRAM-queue state $0773 and JSR $8EDD (the VRAM update/queue transfer); $80E4 JSR $F2D0, $80E7 JSR $8E5C, $80EA JSR $8182, $80ED JSR $8F97 (per-frame game logic: input/player/objects/sound); $80F0-$8138 the frame timers (decrements $0747, $077F, the $0780,X array) and the controller-shift logic; $815C/$8165 write the scroll to $2005 (PPUSCROLL x then y from $073F/$0740); $8168-$817E push $0778, STA $2000, and finally ORA #$80 / STA $2000 to re-enable NMI, then $8181 RTI. What does the job of a NMI: the OAM DMA write to $4014 at $80B3 plus the PPUCTRL/PPUMASK/PPUSCROLL writes, all done once per frame. Emulator proof: trace_writes on CPU $2000 for 60 frames returned 60 writes from PC $808F, 60 from $816F and 60 from $8181 - a full set of PPUCTRL writes every frame - and all three PCs lie inside $8082-$8181. Since the main thread idles at $8057, every frame's hardware/vblank work is this handler.

0x8212.name: GameEngine - per-frame dispatch on GameMode ($0770)
0x8212.notes: The game-mode dispatch. Runs once per frame from the NMI: at CPU $8175 the NMI does JSR $8212, guarded by LDA $0776 / LSR A / BCS (skip) at $816F-$8173, so it only runs when OperMode bit 0 is clear. Entry $8212: LDA $0770 (GameMode) ; JSR $8E04 (jump engine), and the 4-entry target table follows at $8218: $8231 (mode 0 = title screen / attract demo), $AEDC (mode 1 = game / in a level), $838B (mode 2 = victory), $9218 (mode 3 = game over). $8E04 is the jump engine: ASL A / TAY / PLA / STA $04 / PLA / STA $05 / INY / LDA ($04),Y / STA $06 / INY / LDA ($04),Y / STA $07 / JMP ($0006) - it pops the return address (the table at $8218) and uses A as a byte index to fetch the target and JMP indirectly. Both $8231 and $AEDC are themselves secondary dispatchers (each starts LDA $0772 / JSR $8E04). Found with no reference by searching PRG for LDA $0770: the only match in the per-frame path is $8212, which the NMI calls. Emulator proof: play_input/watch on $0770 read 0 on the title/attract screen and flipped to 1 exactly when the second Start began World 1-1; the mapping's LoseLife sets $0770=3 at game over, which is mode 3 -> $9218. Table bytes at $8218: $8231,$AEDC,$838B,$9218.

0x85BF.name: LoadAreaPalette - pick the area's background+sprite palette when a level starts
0x85BF.notes: The routine that loads an area's background and sprite colours at level start. It is step 9 of the level-initialization state machine at $8567 (LDA $073C / JSR $8E04 with the address table at $856D; one of its targets is $85BF). Entry $85BF: LDY $074E (area palette index) ; LDX $85BB,Y (selector table at $85BB = $01,$02,$03,$04) ; STX $0773 (VRAM-buffer selector) ; JMP $8745. The NMI then does at $80B6-$80C3: LDX $0773 / LDA $805A,X / STA $00 / LDA $806D,X / STA $01 / JSR $8EDD, and that writes the selected PRG buffer to the PPU through $2006/$2007. The four selectable buffers are complete [3F 00 20 <32 palette bytes> 00] records in PRG: $8CA4 (selector 1, dark/underground-like), $8CC8 (selector 2, the normal overworld palette used by World 1-1), $8CEC (selector 3), $8D10 (selector 4). Found with no reference: a trace_writes read on the selector table $85BB during a forced World 1-1 reload (time-up death) returned exactly one access - PC $85C5, right after LDX $85BB,Y at $85C2, reading address $85BC (=$85BB+$074E with $074E=1), value 2 - i.e. this routine chose the overworld block for 1-1. Corroboration: a trace_writes read over $8CA0-$8D27 during another reload caught the NMI writer reading $8CC8-$8CEB (PCs $8E96/$8E9C/$8EBB/$8EE2) and copying it to $2007; writing $0773=1 by hand while paused then step_frame 1 swapped the entire level to the $8CA4 palette (pipes blue/pink, ground green - screenshot) and $0773=2 restored the normal overworld colours. $074E read 1 during World 1-1 play.

0x8EDD.name: WriteVRAMBuffer - NMI routine that writes palette/VRAM via $2006/$2007
0x8EDD.notes: The code that actually puts the area palette on the hardware, i.e. the $2006/$2007 writer the task suspected ("possibly from a RAM buffer that the frame interrupt copies"). The NMI calls it at $80C3 with $00/$01 already pointing at the buffer chosen from tables $805A/$806D by the selector $0773. Entry $8EDD: LDX $2002 ; LDY #$00 ; LDA ($00),Y ; BNE $8E92 - a zero first byte ends the transfer with two STA $2005 and RTS. The non-empty path at $8E92: STA $2006 (address high) ; INY ; LDA ($00),Y ; STA $2006 (address low) ; INY ; LDA ($00),Y (control/length) ; ASL A ; PHA ; (bit 7 of the control byte toggles a PPUCTRL bit via $8EA9 JSR $8EED, which stores $0778/$2000) ; ASL A / LSR A / LSR A / TAX (length) ; loop at $8EB6-$8EBF: LDA ($00),Y / STA $2007 / DEX / BNE ; then $8EC1-$8ECB advances the pointer by Y and the next record is processed. For a palette record [3F 00 20 ...] this sets PPUADDR to $3F00 and writes the following 32 bytes to $2007, loading all 8 hardware palettes (4 BG + 4 sprite) in one go. Found with no reference from the trace of the palette data (read PCs $8E96/$8E9C/$8EBB/$8EE2) and from a search for LDA #$3F / STA $2006, which occurs only at $8ECD in this routine. Proven: forcing $0773=1,2 by hand and stepping one frame changed the rendered palette accordingly.
